requirements.requirement: node1 becomes the DNS resolver for the shared private network and authoritatively answers inventory.internal with node2's address
requirements.summary: VyOS node1 was configured with 'service dns forwarding' listening on 10.100.50.10, allow-from 10.100.50.0/24, and an authoritative-domain zone for inventory.internal with an apex A record pointing to node2's address 10.100.50.11 (ttl 300). Committed and saved. dig @10.100.50.10 inventory.internal +short returned 10.100.50.11 both before and after a full node1 reboot, confirming persistence.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other DNS queries upstream
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with 'name-server 10.100.50.1' as the upstream forwarder. dig @10.100.50.10 example.com +short returned real upstream A records, both pre- and post-reboot, confirming forwarding works and persists.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve DNS through node1
requirements.summary: nmcli was used on node2 and node3 to set ipv4.dns to 10.100.50.10 and ipv4.ignore-auto-dns yes, applied live; /etc/resolv.conf on both nodes shows nameserver 10.100.50.10. getent hosts confirmed inventory.internal -> 10.100.50.11 and example.com resolving via upstream, verified both before and after each node's reboot.

overall_summary: The executor correctly made node1 (VyOS) an authoritative+forwarding DNS resolver: it answers inventory.internal with node2's private address and forwards all other queries to the upstream 10.100.50.1 nameserver. node2 and node3 were both repointed to node1 as their sole DNS resolver via NetworkManager, and resolution was verified end-to-end. All three nodes were also rebooted with clear boot-identity transitions and full recovery of DNS service/config observed pre- and post-reboot, satisfying the restart evidence protocol with only a minor caveat: node2 shows a failed NetworkManager-wait-online.service after its reboot that was not investigated.
limitations: node2's after-executor snapshot shows a newly-failed NetworkManager-wait-online.service post-reboot that was not present at baseline and was not addressed or explained by the executor, though it did not prevent DNS resolution from working.

Restart/persistence is not an explicit requirement of the public task contract, so restart evidence quality informs confidence and hygiene rather than the satisfied/not_satisfied status of the three material DNS requirements.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map directly to material task outcomes: the VyOS DNS forwarding/authoritative-zone config (cmd-04e6cce2faaa4f56) and its commit/save, the nmcli DNS changes on node2/node3 (cmd-5ed6a73f81a240f4, cmd-f970799fd2664732), and the three node reboots executed to satisfy the provider-wide restart evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unrestored mutations, troubleshooting residue, or destructive commands were observed; most preceding commands were read-only discovery of VyOS template/conf_mode syntax. One post-restart artifact stands out: node2's after-executor snapshot shows NetworkManager-wait-online.service in a failed state, which was not present at baseline and was not investigated or remediated by the executor after the reboot — a minor unaddressed residue from the restart, though DNS resolution itself was verified working regardless.
